text:
A young tiger named Raja lived deep in the forest, where he spent his days hunting and roaming. One evening, the wind carried the most incredible smell from a nearby village—spices, rice, and something magical he'd never known. Curious, he crept closer and saw a grandmother stirring a huge pot of biryani. He watched her every move: the layering, the dum, the careful timing. From that night, he couldn't stop thinking about it.

Raja decided he had to learn. He practised in secret, using paws instead of hands, a hollow log instead of a handi. He gathered rice from the edge of the fields, traded forest herbs for spices with a kind old cook, and learned to control the fire with his breath. His first attempts were disasters—burnt rice, raw meat, spices everywhere. But he kept trying, night after night, until one day the smell rising from his log was perfect.

Word spread through the forest. Animals came from far and wide to taste Raja's biryani, and even the village grandmother heard the rumours. She trekked into the woods, tasted a spoonful, and smiled. "You've got it," she said. From then on, Raja became the forest's beloved chef, proving that passion and patience can turn anyone—even a tiger—into a master.
